description: The National Emissions Inventory (NEI) is the EPA's estimate of air emissions of criteria pollutants, criteria precursors and hazardous air pollutants from all air emission sources in the United States. It is produced by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency every three years, mainly from data submitted by State, Local and Tribal air agencies through the Emissions Inventory System (EIS) and blended with EPA estimates. Coverage is national: point sources are fixed facilities such as large industrial plants, electric power plants and airports, reported under the thresholds of the Air Emissions Reporting Rule; nonpoint sources are county or tribal totals for small sources such as residential heating and solvent use, with all fires counted as nonpoint since 2020; onroad emissions are computed with the MOVES model except in California, which supplies its own; nonroad mobile sources are also included. Data are available free online from the EPA inventory pages, whose overview was last updated on 26 March 2026. Caveats: values are estimates whose methods differ by source category and agency, point source reporting depends on thresholds, and releases lag the inventory year. For simulation it gives facility-level emission profiles for exposure and environmental impact analyses of industrial and energy sites and a baseline for adaptation scenarios. It is related to the EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program record in this catalogue, which covers greenhouse gases.
